tasks.short: Monitor energy design and construction issues

steps.what: Review current energy-related design or construction issues and their revisions in {PROJECT}, filtering by building system, owner and due date
Inspect actual design details and construction conditions affecting insulation, controls, equipment efficiency and sustainable design
Monitor energy engineering and management issues by assessing their consequences and discussing workable corrections with the responsible designers or builders
Write and check the final actual issue update in {PROJECT}; reuse issue identity and revision fields while preserving unresolved findings
Commit the exact checked issue update in {PROJECT}

tasks.design: Test native issue filters and revision-linked update fields in {PROJECT}. The engineer inspects actual conditions, decides their energy implications and checks the completed issue update before committing it; a planned correction is never automatically marked complete.
tasks.previous_blocker: Issue navigation and re-entry of existing identifiers can obscure current revisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native issue views and reusable record fields can narrow navigation and duplicate headers.
tasks.still_hard: Construction deviations and their energy effect need physical and engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer identifies whether the installed detail can achieve the intended performance.

ambition.what: No autonomous design approval or closure.

tasks.altitude: Less issue navigation; unchanged technical accountability.

reach.learn: Tie actual correction evidence to the relevant design revision.

evidence.claim: Issue-register filters and revision fields can reduce repeated navigation and identifier entry.

assumptions: Boundary is the engineer's issue monitoring and record, excluding construction work and formal design approval. No physical or other-role time saving is claimed.

Designers and site staff produce actual issue ID, building system, location, revision, owner and observed status. The engineer checks them in s1-s2 and captures findings in s4. Missing issue data are investigated manually; scheduled correction is not completion.
Native configuration first; illustrative shares are not measured. Final s4 checking follows completed wording and binds the exact issue, revision and actual status; edits void the commit gate.
unknowns: Whether native issue filters and header reuse already work
research_questions: How much issue navigation and duplicate header capture remains?

already_counted.description: Issue relevance review and actual update checking remain in s1 and s4.

incremental.description: Maintain issue views and revised field mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Final actual issue update checked in s4; any edit requires rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Navigation and headers save 8.4 gross hours less 1.4 upkeep for 7 net. Already configured views give zero benefit. Inspection, discussion, technical assessment and commit stay counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Audit energy use and conservation measures

steps.what: Conduct the site portion of the energy audit: inspect systems, operating practices and actual measurement conditions and record observations
Obtain and verify bills, meter periods, tariffs, weather and occupancy information for the energy audit

Evaluate energy use and identify conservation and cost-reduction measures using the energy-audit category of {OTHER}; calculate explicit consumption, tariff and measure scenarios while judging practical feasibility
Write and check the completed audit report in {DOCS}, including measure interactions, estimated costs, uncertainties, evidence and exact client recipient
Save the exact checked audit report in {DOCS}
Send the exact versioned audit report to the checked client through {EMAIL}

tasks.design: Test native calculation templates in the energy-audit category of {OTHER} for explicit consumption and tariff scenarios. The engineer collects actual evidence, checks feasibility and writes and reviews the final report before separately saving and sending it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated unit, tariff and scenario arithmetic can be rebuilt for each audit.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calculation structures can reuse formulas with checked job-specific inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Occupancy changes, interacting measures and operational constraints complicate claimed benefits.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides whether a measure can work in the actual building.

ambition.what: No autonomous investment recommendation or regulatory filing.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic, unchanged audit judgement.

reach.task: Explain operating constraints on conservation measures
reach.learn: Test whether a proposed measure can be maintained in practice.

evidence.claim: Explicit energy and tariff calculations can use native formulas while practical measure selection remains engineering work.

assumptions: Boundary is an energy audit through client report, excluding implementation and formal statutory submissions. No measured savings in the building or company baseline are claimed.

The engineer captures site observations in s1 and verifies meter ID, interval, energy quantity, unit, bill period, tariff, occupancy and weather provenance in s2. Building records supply raw values, not free cleaned inputs. Missing data are clarified and entered manually; measure assumptions and interaction checks remain in s3-s4.

Native configuration first. Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. This audit's calculations are distinct from a separate energy-data analysis assignment in 18159; where the same outputs are reused, do not count a second calculation saving. Final s4 checking binds exact report and client after completion; edits void approval.
unknowns: Whether native audit formulas already cover the work
Quality of interval data and operational context
research_questions: Which repeated arithmetic remains after native audit configuration?

already_counted.description: Calculation review, feasibility and final audit report remain in s3-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain formula tests and tariff unit mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Final audit report checked in s4; edits void approval.
Same final audit report checked in s4 and saved unchanged in s5, to the exact checked client recipient.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated calculations save 8 gross less 1.5 upkeep for 6.5 net. Already configured formulas give zero added benefit. Site work, data capture, report judgement and actions retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify and enter energy series, meter scope, units, time zones, gaps and operating context before analysis
Create graphical representations of energy data using the engineering-analysis category of {OTHER}; aggregate explicit intervals, label units and prepare load profiles and stated normalisations
Analyze and interpret energy graphs, check sensitivity and distinguish operational explanations from unsupported causal claims
Write and check the final graph notes, definitions, caveats and source references in the engineering-analysis category of {OTHER}
Save the exact checked energy analysis snapshot in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native interval aggregation and reusable load-profile views in the engineering-analysis category of {OTHER}. The engineer verifies actual source series, interprets the results and checks final graph definitions before saving the snapshot; no model asserts why energy changed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated aggregation, axis setup and unit labelling can be manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Native engineering views and explicit settings can repeat those operations consistently.
tasks.still_hard: Bad meter scope and changed operating conditions can invalidate a neat chart.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer knows which comparisons are physically meaningful.

ambition.what: Review a fresh operating-period load profile when data quality supports it.

tasks.altitude: Less graph setup, more attention to actual causes and data limits.

reach.learn: Connect operating events to time-aligned measurements without assuming causation.

evidence.claim: Native aggregation and plot settings can automate repeated graph construction, not causal interpretation.

assumptions: Boundary is a standalone energy-series analysis and saved output, not the audit in 20855. Shared datasets may be inputs; the same graph-building action must not be counted twice in a team roll-up.

Meter records supply meter ID, timestamp, interval, quantity, unit and quality flag; facilities staff supply actual operating events. The engineer checks scope, gaps, time zone and normalisation fields in s1, including manual entry where exports fail. Missing observations remain missing and are not silently interpolated.

Native configuration first; shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Runtime earns no saving. Final s4 checking follows completed graphs and notes and binds source version and settings; edits invalidate the save gate.
unknowns: Whether load profiles are already generated natively
research_questions: How much actual analyst setup does native graph configuration remove?

already_counted.description: Graph review, engineering interpretation and final notes remain in s2-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain aggregation settings and investigate changed meter fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final dataset version, settings, graphs and notes checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated plot setup saves 22 gross hours less 2 upkeep for 20 net. Already configured views give zero benefit. Source capture, interpretation and saving remain counted.

tasks.short: Train personnel or clients in energy management

steps.what: Prepare energy-management training around the audience's actual meters, schedules and controls; adapt approved examples in {DOCS} while reusing slide layouts
Train personnel or clients on energy management, demonstrate appropriate readings and discuss their actual operating questions
Write and check actual attendance and follow-up learning needs in the existing {LMS} session item
Save the exact checked training record in {LMS}

tasks.design: Test reusable native training layouts in {DOCS}, using existing checked energy examples as inputs. Keep actual teaching, observation of understanding and post-session capture human; the {LMS} record is checked only after training occurs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated training layout can accompany otherwise necessary audience adaptation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document styles can reuse format without claiming new energy analysis.
tasks.still_hard: Operating staff need to understand what readings mean in their own work.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises mistaken control assumptions during questions and demonstrations.

ambition.what: No expanded operator authorisation or certification.

tasks.altitude: Less slide setup, unchanged training responsibility.

reach.task: Use energy readings during daily operations
reach.learn: Explain readings with the actual control and operating context.

evidence.claim: Reusable training layouts can reduce format setup while audience adaptation and teaching stay human.

assumptions: Boundary is training and an ordinary existing session record, not producing the energy analysis in 18159, granting operating access or changing controls. Reusing existing graphs earns no second calculation credit.

The client supplies audience and operating context; the engineer selects existing checked examples and writes explanations in s1. Actual attendee identity, date and follow-up needs are captured after s2 in s3. Missing attendance is clarified manually, not inferred from enrolment.
Native configuration first; shares are illustrative, not measured. Final s3 checking binds the actual completed training entry before save. No material-send or separate approval ceremony is invented.
unknowns: Whether the existing training layouts already cover repeated setup
research_questions: What actual format setup remains after native styles?

already_counted.description: Actual training preparation and material checking remain in s1.

incremental.description: Maintain approved energy-training layouts and examples.

approvals.approved_version: Actual post-training record checked in s3; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated layout saves 3.75 gross less 0.75 upkeep for 3 net. Existing layouts give zero gain. Teaching, actual capture and saving retain their effort.
